# Governance Quality Standards

This directory contains standards governing how quality obligations — non-functional requirements and universal/negative invariants — are specified and verified across the enterprise. They are the non-behavioral counterparts to the behavioral (BDD) requirement practice, and together they make every requirement axis of [ADR-GOV-011](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-011-architecture-pipeline-operating-model.md) accountable.

[standards/governance/quality/README.md#std-gov-qa-001-non-functional-requirement-specification-standard]

### STD-GOV-QA-001: Non-Functional Requirement Specification Standard

Mandates the quality-attribute-scenario schema for every NFR, the behavioral-vs-systemic classification rule, and the requirement that each systemic NFR bind to an operational, CI-invoked test harness.
page_texts.5:
[standards/governance/quality/README.md#std-gov-qa-002-universal-property--invariant-verification-standard]

### STD-GOV-QA-002: Universal Property & Invariant Verification Standard

Mandates that universal/negative properties ("for all / never") be registered as `INV-*` invariants and verified by an architecture-fitness or property-based harness, with the design-vs-implementer ownership split for self-gating (e.g. authorization) invariants.
page_texts.6:
[standards/governance/quality/README.md#purpose]

## Purpose

These standards ensure:
- Quality attributes are specified uniformly and measurably, not asserted in prose
- Systemic NFRs and negative invariants are verified by real, CI-invoked harnesses
- Compliance-critical negatives (PHI, authorization) are provable, auditable requirements
